### 8–16s — CN09-DIAGRAM-1
Voiceover: 01 · CONDITION — Which barrier is being changed?. Use participant and field evidence to name the constraint—time, space, tools, care, legal access, production, archive, education, market, or safety—without inventing deficit narratives.

Treatment: vertical reveal with source footer

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 16–24s — CN09-DIAGRAM-2
Voiceover: 02 · POWER — Who defines success?. Allocate governance among participants, practitioners, community authorities, staff, independent reviewers, and funder; disclose conflicts and create appeal and correction routes.

Treatment: slow evidence push; no synthetic parallax

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 24–32s — CN09-DIAGRAM-3
Voiceover: 03 · RIGHT — What do recipients retain?. Separate grant conditions, IP, name and likeness, documentation, data, confidentiality, cultural knowledge, publication, archive, and post-program access.

Treatment: vertical reveal with source footer

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 32–40s — CN09-DIAGRAM-4
Voiceover: 04 · CONTINUE — What remains when funding stops?. Plan unrestricted assets, maintained tools, open or governed curricula, participant networks, preserved records, successor funding, and an ethical closure route.

Treatment: slow evidence push; no synthetic parallax

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
